12.text: In most cases the keˊlet begin by entering the body of the shaman.

13.text: This is marked with some change in his manner of beating the drum, which

14.text: becomes faster and more violent; but the chief mark is a series of new sounds,

15.text: supposed to be peculiar to the keˊlet. The shaman shakes his head violently,

16.text: producing with his lips a peculiar chattering noise, not unlike a man who is

17.text: shivering with cold.¹ He shouts hysterically, and in a changed voice utters

18.text: strange, prolonged shrieks, such as “O to, to, to, to,” or “I pi, pi, pi, pi,” —

19.text: all of which are supposed to characterize the voice of the keˊlet. He often

20.text: imitates the cries of various animals and birds which are supposed to be his

21.text: particular assistants. If the shaman is only a “single-bodied” one, — that is,

22.text: has no ventriloquistic power, — the keˊlet will proceed to sing and beat the

23.text: drum by means of his body. The only difference will be in the timbre of the

24.text: voice, which will sound harsh and unnatural, as becomes supernatural beings.

25.text: VENTRILOQUISM AND OTHER TRICKS. — With other shamans the keˊlet

26.text: appear all at once as the “separate voices.” They manifest themselves with

27.text: sounds and shrieks of the same harsh and unnatural character, and these are

28.text: located outside the body of the shaman. After that a varied exhibition begins,

29.text: in which the performance of the shaman far transcends anything attainable

30.text: by a person of ordinary powers.

31.text: The Chukchee ventriloquists display great skill, and could with credit to

32.text: themselves carry on a contest with the best artists of the kind of civilized

33.text: countries. The “separate voices” of their calling come from all sides of the

34.text: room, changing their place to the complete illusion of their listeners. Some

35.text: voices are at first faint, as if coming from afar; as they gradually approach,

36.text: they increase in volume, and at last they rush into the room, pass through

37.text: it and out, decreasing, and dying away in the remote distance. Other voices

38.text: come from above, pass through the room and seem to go underground, where

39.text: they are heard as if from the depths of the earth. Tricks of this kind are

40.text: played also with the voices of animals and birds, and even with the howling

41.text: of the tempest, producing a most weird effect.
